title: Falling in Reverse, Corey Taylor & Serj Tankian Top Hot Hard Rock Songs Chart With ‘Joseph’
summary: The band lands its seventh No. 1 with the high-profile collaboration.
body: Falling in Reverse rules Billboard ’s Hot Hard Rock Songs chart for a seventh time, debuting at No. 1 on the Sept. 26-dated list with “Joseph,” a collaboration with Corey Taylor and Serj Tankian . In the week ending Sept. 17, “Joseph” totaled 2.2 million chart-eligible streams, 49,000 radio audience impressions and 3,000 sold in the United States, according to Luminate. That’s despite a partial week of data, as the song was released Sept. 14. Falling in Reverse topped the inaugural Hot Hard Rock Songs list in June 2020 with “Popular Monster.” Prior to “Joseph,” the band most recently ruled with its Jelly Roll collaboration “All My Life” for 11 weeks in 2024. With seven No. 1s, Falling in Reverse moves back into a tie with Bring Me the Horizon for the most. The latter last led in July with “Dehumanized.” As for Taylor, “Joseph” is his second leader as a soloist, following his featured turn on Motionless in White ’s “Playing God” in May. Slipknot , with him as its frontman, has a No. 1 on the chart, “The Chapeltown Rag,” in 2021. Tankian snags his first ruler solo, while his band System of a Down led with “Protect the Land” in 2020. title: YouTube is finally giving you more control over what shows up on your Home feed
summary: You'll be able to save separate feeds for different interests, moods, and routines.
body: TL;DR YouTube is turning its earlier Custom Feed experiment into a full feature that lets you build recommendation feeds with conversational prompts. You can save multiple feeds for different interests, moods, or routines, and YouTube will keep them updated with fresh recommendations. Custom Feeds are coming soon to users in the US across mobile, web, and TVs. YouTube’s Home tab has always had a funny way of overreacting. Watch one random woodworking video, and suddenly the algorithm can decide you’ve found your new life’s calling. Last year, YouTube started testing a way to fight that problem by letting some users tell an AI chatbot what they actually wanted to see. Now that experiment is growing up, with YouTube officially announcing Custom Feeds, giving viewers a more direct way to build separate recommendation feeds around specific interests, routines, or moods. The original test added a “Your Custom Feed” chip beside Home for select users. You could prompt YouTube to adjust what appeared there, essentially correcting the recommendation algorithm instead of waiting for your watch history to do the job.

title: Arctic Sea Ice Reaches 2026 Annual Minimum Extent
summary: Arctic sea ice reached its annual minimum extent on Sept. 12, according to NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) at the University of Colorado Boulder. The ice covered an estimated 1.78 million square miles (4.6 million square kilometers), tying 2008, 2010, and 2025 for the 10th-lo…
body: Daily images of ice cover in the Arctic Ocean show sea ice melting around the pole from March 15, 2026 to Sept. 12, 2026. Trent Schindler/NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio Arctic sea ice reached its annual minimum extent on Sept. 12, according to NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) at the University of Colorado Boulder. The ice covered an estimated 1.78 million square miles (4.6 million square kilometers), tying 2008, 2010, and 2025 for the 10th-lowest minimum in the satellite record. The 2026 minimum is consistent with patterns observed in the satellite record. The past 20 years, from 2007 through 2026, have produced the 20 lowest annual Arctic sea ice minimum extents observed since continuous satellite measurements began in late 1978. Arctic sea ice grows during the dark, cold autumn and winter and retreats as temperatures rise during spring and summer, typically reaching its lowest extent in September. Weather conditions can cause substantial differences in the amount of ice that melts from one summer to another. Over the last decade, for example, increased cloud cover has prevented solar radiation from further accelerating the melt of sea ice, according…

title: Google Recorder could soon fix its biggest drawback for power users
summary: A toggle may let you automatically save all future recordings to your internal storage.
body: TL;DR The Google Recorder app is working on a new toggle to make audio recordings accessible from the device’s native storage. Audio recordings in the app are currently saved in a sandboxed folder and hidden from file manager apps, unless you save them manually. This upcoming toggle could remember your choice even when you clear data or set up the app on a new device. The Pixel-exclusive Google Recorder has everything you can ask for from an audio recording app. However, managing saved recordings is anything but simple. Recorder can store audio files in the cloud or directly in the app. Accessing these files from your native file manager app is cumbersome and requires you to download them via Android’s share sheet. A future update to Google Recorder could finally make things a tad easier. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. title: I’ve used Razr phones for 20 years, and Motorola’s secret weapon hasn’t changed
summary: Motorola understands who buys its phones.
body: I’ve used Motorola phones longer than I’d like to admit. The Nokia 5160 I carried around in high school will always hold a special place in my heart, but Motorola soon became my preferred brand. I remember how jealous I was when my parents bought StarTACs. It’s hard to describe what a shift that device was for cell phones. Moto proved that the phones in our pockets could be smaller and more stylish, and the company wasn’t done there. The original Razr was a revelation when it was released in 2004. You didn’t want to buy anything else at the time, and it was hard to go anywhere without seeing someone use one. It’s why Motorola’s recent success isn’t a surprise. The company has maintained a consistent theme over the last two decades, and it doesn’t take much to see where that all began and how it translates perfectly to this current crop of Razrs.

title: The Sleenova SoundMask fixed my biggest issue with sleep earbuds
summary: Speakers next to your ears instead of inside them is a big deal for a side sleeper like me.
body: I’ve tested a handful of sleep earbuds over the years, and no matter how small they get, I haven’t found a pair that doesn’t create pressure in my ears while sleeping on my side, which can be uncomfortable. The Sleenova SoundMask avoids that problem with speakers built into the sides of a sleep mask that sits next to your ears. After a few nights with it, it became a pretty reliable tool for getting a good night’s rest, with its own tradeoffs to sleep earbuds. No more sore ears The SoundMask is very comfortable. Rather than pressing flat against your eyelids, there’s a contoured cavity that lifts the fabric off your eyes entirely, so you can blink and move your eyes freely without anything rubbing against them. There is ample padding around the eyes and nose, so that I could sleep face-down into a pillow without discomfort. It also blocks out light surprisingly well. I couldn’t see anything while wearing it, even in a fully lit room.

title: Qualcomm could finally fix a major issue with PC emulation on Android
summary: Does this mean we won't have to download custom Turnip drivers anymore?
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR Qualcomm reportedly plans to improve support for PC game emulation on Android devices via its official GPU drivers. The company is also apparently thinking about bringing DirectX12 support to its GPU drivers on Android. This could potentially result in better performance and improved compatibility for PC games running on Android. There’s no shortage of PC gaming emulators on Android, allowing you to run a variety of games on your phone, tablet, or handheld . However, you often need to install unofficial GPU drivers for the best performance and compatibility. Fortunately, it sounds like Qualcomm could bring improvements in this regard. Tech YouTuber Geekerwan reports that Qualcomm plans to improve support for PC game emulation on Android via its official GPU drivers. The YouTuber noted that they tried Cyberpunk 2077 and Black Myth: Wukong on a phone with a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series chip. They reported that both games ran properly in DirectX12 mode using a translation layer.

title: Facing trouble with the Home Up Good Lock module? You’re not alone, and a fix is coming

body: TL;DR Home Up users may be unable to back up their settings if they have set custom folder label colors. Samsung is working on a fix and will roll it out in a future software update. For now, users can revert folder label colors to their default settings and create backups. As feature-packed as Samsung’s One UI already is, you can use Good Lock modules to get even more customization options for your phone. Modules like Home Up offer deep home screen customization, and you can even back up your settings and restore them later. However, there appears to be an issue with Home Up’s backup option that prevents users from restoring their settings. If you’re facing a similar issue on your Galaxy phone, you can rest easy knowing Samsung is already working on a fix. According to a post on the Samsung Community forums, the Home Up module’s backup feature doesn’t work properly if you’ve selected custom colors for folder labels. A Samsung Community moderator shared this information after a user reported that Home Up keeps deleting their backup file and telling them it’s “broken.”

title: Google Sheets now plays more nicely with your imported Excel spreadsheets
summary: Sheets also brings improvements for handling pivot tables.
body: TL;DR Google Sheets now lets users drag and drop rows or columns in pivot tables. It also maintains data hierarchy when moving rows or columns with nested child items. It now also preserves custom-sorted pivot tables when importing Excel spreadsheets. The last few months have been really great for Google Sheets users. Google has steadily rolled out new updates and features, introduced useful add-ons , and improved support for pivot tables . Now, it’s making it easier for users to manipulate pivot tables directly in Sheets. Google announced today that Sheets can now preserve custom sorting in pivot tables imported from Excel spreadsheets. Previously, Sheets reverted pivot tables to a standard alphanumeric sort order. However, it will now maintain any custom sort you’ve applied within Excel so you can easily move between the two apps. Exporting a Sheets file to an Excel spreadsheet also maintains the exact sorting order of your pivot tables.

summary: Catherine O’Connell-Cooper, APXS Strategic Planner and Payload Uplink/Downlink Lead, University New Brunswick, NB, Canada Earth planning date: Friday, Sept. 11, 2026 This week we had two planning days (Tuesday and Friday), as Monday was Labor Day in North America, where many of the Curiosity team a…
body: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 3 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5010-5015: Checking out the Bands NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this image, showing the path ahead. title: The smart glasses market has more than doubled in the last year, with Meta dominating

body: Credit: Chase Bernath / Android Authority TL;DR Global AI glasses shipments jumped 263% year over year in H1 2026, according to Counterpoint Research. Display-less models accounted for 96% of shipments, with Meta holding a dominant 94% share of that segment. Shipments of AR glasses surged 449% year over year, albeit from a low base. Smart glasses might still feel like a niche category of tech, but they seem to be selling at a much faster clip than they were a year ago. Global AI glasses shipments jumped 263% year over year in the first half of 2026, and the vast majority weren’t AR specs. Counterpoint Research’s latest Intelligent Eyewear Market Tracker attributes most of that growth to the cheaper, more mature display-less category, which includes products such as the Ray-Ban Meta AI Glasses.
